key_insight: Random data splits substantially overestimate machine-learning performance in perovskite photovoltaics because duplicated device recipes let models memorize prior examples instead of learning transferable physics.
engineering_relevance: Using provenance-grouped evaluation gives a more realistic benchmark for solar-cell design models and better identifies which architectures can generalize to unseen institutions and future device recipes.
method: Mapped institutional provenance in the Perovskite Database.
Built a hierarchy of grouped splits to isolate duplicates, publications, and institutions.
Benchmarked 13 models under progressively stricter evaluation settings.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that nearly two-thirds of curated devices have an exact recipe duplicate, and that model rankings shift sharply when evaluation moves from random splits to unseen institutions and future discoveries.
watch_item: Provenance-grouped protocols depend on accurate database metadata and duplicate detection, so incomplete records could still bias the evaluation.
paper_title: Provenance-grouped protocol for evaluating machine learning in perovskite photovoltaics
